title: Slices of an integer action site recover the original localized sites
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $s:C\to C$ be a site automorphism with chosen inverse, preserving pullbacks and coverings; use its coherent integer powers. Define $D$ to have the objects of $C$ and arrows $(n,f):U\to V$ with $n\in\mathbf Z$ and $f:U\to s^nV$, identity $(0,1)$ and composition $(m,h)\circ(n,f)=(n+m,s^n(h)\circ f)$. Give $D$ the Grothendieck topology generated by degree-zero $J$-coverings. For each $V\in C$ the degree-zero inclusion $j_V:C/V\to D/V$ is an equivalence of sites, where the slice topologies are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A quasi-inverse sends $(n,f:W\to s^nV)$ to $(s^{-n}W,s^{-n}f:s^{-n}W\to V)$, and sends a slice morphism $(k,h)$ from $(n,f)$ to $(m,g)$ (so $n=k+m$) to $s^{-n}h$. For every sheaf of commutative rings $A$ on $D/V$, restriction along $j_V$ induces an additive equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}_{D/V}(A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}_{C/V}(j_V^*A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], whose action on sections and morphisms is ordinary degree-zero restriction.

proof.text: Use ShiftedHom unit and associativity coherence to prove the laws of the displayed pair category and its degree-zero inclusion. The projection of the slice relation proves the degree identity.

The inclusion on slices is fully faithful: a morphism between two degree-zero slice objects has degree zero, and ShiftedHom.homEquiv recovers its unique underlying ordinary morphism. The power isomorphism of degree minus the structure-arrow degree gives an isomorphism from the included normalized object to every slice object. Conjugating by these isomorphisms and applying the explicit fully faithful preimage constructs the inverse functor. Its counit and the lifted unit give an equivalence. Counit naturality, read in the sigma type of arrows, identifies the inverse map with the stated inverse-power formula.

Degree-zero restriction and generated direct image are inverse order isomorphisms between sieves at each object: a degree-zero composite forces its first factor to have degree zero, while every arbitrary arrow is a degree-zero normalized arrow preceded by a source isomorphism. The naturality square of the power isomorphisms identifies restriction of pullback along a power isomorphism, after an ordinary shift, with the original restricted sieve. Every shift is continuous for the generated topology, by its preservation of generating covers and Mathlib induced-topology minimality. Therefore degree-zero restriction transports the base generated topology to an actual topology on the action category. Conversely, direct image transports any topology on the action category to a topology on the base: it preserves the top sieve and commutes with pullback along ordinary arrows; the local-character axiom follows by factoring an arrow in a direct-image sieve. Applying both least-topology properties proves that the prescribed action topology covers exactly the sieves whose degree-zero restrictions cover in the base. This argument handles arbitrary precoverages stable under the prescribed shifts and does not require constructing a pretopology on the action category.

Mathlib Sieve.overEquiv_functorPushforward_post identifies the direct image on slice sieves with direct image on underlying sieves. The preceding sieve criterion gives preservation and reflection of slice covers by the inclusion. The equivalence counit and the double-direct-image formula give the same property for the inverse. Both equivalences are representably flat, so Mathlib cover preservation proves continuity in both directions. Apply SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence with the identity ring map in the inclusion direction and the ring morphism induced by the counit in the reverse direction. Counit and unit naturality give its compatibility identities. The resulting restriction functor is an equivalence; its preservation of addition is the componentwise identity.
